graph/formula: Take a formula: x times z, plus c, all squared. A computational graph breaks it into simple operations, one node each.
graph/mul: First, a multiply node. It takes x and z, and sends out their product. Call it q.
graph/add: A wire carries q into an add node, which adds c. Call that r.
graph/sq: Then a square node turns r into f, the output. Three operations, three nodes.
graph/pieces: Any formula breaks down into a handful of such pieces: add, multiply, max, e to the x, and square.
forward/inputs: To evaluate the graph, give the inputs values: x is two, z is three, and c is minus four.
forward/mul: Values flow forward, from the inputs toward the output. The multiply gives two times three: six.
forward/add: The add gives six plus minus four: two.
forward/sq: And the square gives two squared, four. So f is four.
forward/ready: The order is forced. A node can run only once every value it needs has arrived, so the add waits for the multiply, and the square waits for the add.
more/max: The other pieces work the same way. A max node passes on the larger of its inputs: the max of one and minus two is one.
more/exp: An exp node raises e to its input. e to the one is about two point seven two.
more/mul: And z feeds a second node too: the multiply. Two point seven two times minus two is about minus five point four four.
